study_type_evidence.quote: Mice were treated according to their assigned groups (i.e., CLA-coated PTX-SPIONs@HRH or commercial PTX), with each group having 3 mice (n = 3), and euthanized over 24 h
A lung adenocarcinoma (A549) cell line was employed to assess the viability of the cells treated with CLA-coated PTX-SPIONs@HRH, over 72 h.
study_type_evidence.section: METHODS (Anti-proliferative Activity Assessment on Lung Adenocarcinoma)

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: athymic (MF1-nu/nu) female nude mice, 18-22 g, 4-6 weeks old, bearing subcutaneous A549 lung tumor xenografts
in_vivo_species.quote: Athymic (MF1-nu/nu) female nude mice weighing 18-22 g (4-6 weeks old) were sourced and housed at the Wits Research Animal Facility

in_vitro_detail: A549 lung adenocarcinoma MTT anti-proliferation assay over 72 h (25, 50, 100 μg/mL); cellular uptake and internalisation of FITC-labelled nanoformulation in A549 cells by fluorescence microscopy; VEGF-A quantification by ELISA in human dermal microvascular endothelial cells (HMEC-1) treated with 50 μg/mL; cell-free dialysis-membrane PTX release study at pH 6.8 and pH 7.4 over 24 h.

concentration_time_figure.locator: Figure 10 (also Figure 4 for in vitro release)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Plasma pharmacokinetic profile showing the concentration of PTX quantified from 0.5 to 24 h following SC injection of CLA-coated PTX-SPIONs@HRH and commercial PTX formulation.
concentration_time_figure.note: Figure 10 plots plasma PTX concentration against time (0.5-24 h) after a single SC dose, n = 3. Figure 4 separately plots in vitro cumulative percentage PTX release against time at pH 6.8 and pH 7.4 over 24 h, which is a release-versus-time curve rather than a plasma concentration-time curve.

bioanalytical_method: High performance liquid chromatography with UV detection at 227 nm (Flexar LC UV/VIS, PerkinElmer), after liquid-liquid extraction of plasma with 1.25% v/v ethanol in diethyl ether and docetaxel as internal standard; Waters C18 column (250 x 3.9 mm, 5 μm), 20 μL injection, 1.9 mL/min
bioanalytical_quote: A validated rapid and sensitive high pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) method was employed for the quantification of PTX from plasma using a liquid-liquid extraction technique.
notes: UNIT-HEADER CHECK: the PK table has two separate columns, 'T1/2 (h)' and 'Kel (h-1)'. The half-life values recorded here (17.1 h and 9.0 h) come from the column named T1/2 (h) and are confirmed in the Results text as half-lives ('The half-life (T1/2) of commercial PTX was estimated to be 9.0 h'). The elimination rate constants Kel = 0.03 h-1 (nanoformulation) and Kel = 0.07 h-1 (Taxol) are recorded verbatim here and were NOT converted to half-lives. The paper names no kinetic phase for T1/2, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified' and half_life_elimination is left 'not reported', even though the adjacent Kel column is labelled 'elimination rate constant' in the table footnote. Dosing was subcutaneous, so an absorption phase exists and the body states 'PTX from CLA-coated PTX-SPIONs@HRH is slowly absorbed and released into plasma following SC injection', but no absorption half-life was fitted or reported. The PK measurand is paclitaxel, not the HRH peptide. Plasma sampling was destructive (mice euthanized at each of t = 0.5, 1, 4, 8, 24 h) with n = 3 per group. The antitumor study used a 10-fold lower PTX dose for Taxol (1.2 mg/kg) than the nanoformulation dose (12 mg/kg), matched to the 10% drug loading capacity; the PK study states 'equivalent PTX dosage' without giving a number.
